content.text: {"summary":"You have a strong, well-referenced mission rationale for GBR monitoring. Your project plan is feasible with a Gantt chart, and your report is well-structured. To progress to Part 2, you need to add quantitative technical work and contingency planning, especially hand calculations for orbits and coverage.","criteria":{"C1":"You clearly defined your reef bleaching mission on p2, linking it to Australian benefit and users like marine scientists. To stay at Accomplished, keep this clarity and depth for Part 2.","C2":"You presented a feasible plan with a Gantt Chart on p3 and explained tasks like Background Research on p4. To reach Accomplished, add contingency and variation planning and integrate your source rationale directly into the narrative, not just in Useful Links.","C3":"You have completed literature review and STK tutorials 1-4 on p4, which is good preparation. To reach Accomplished, you need quantitative preliminary results with hand calculations for orbit, launch, coverage and link budget to supplement STK, as missing on p4.","C4":"Your report on p2-p3 with headings Mission Concept & Rationale and Project Plan is clear, well-written and consistently formatted with matching citations. Maintain this standard for Part 2."},"next_steps":["On p4, add 1-2 pages of hand calculations for a sun-synchronous orbit, revisit coverage, and link budget to complement STK results.","Revise your p3 Gantt plan to include 2 weeks buffer for STK/Orbit iteration and define contingency if launch options change.","Integrate your source list into the methodology on p4 by justifying why Asner Hawaii and specific STK tutorials inform your payload choice."]}
